key_insight: VLA-JEPA replaces pixel-anchored latent-action objectives with a JEPA-style, leakage-free latent world model that predicts action-relevant future states in latent space, preventing appearance bias and nuisance motion from driving the representation.
problem_solved: Pretraining VLA policies often learn spurious pixel-level correlations and leak irrelevant visual information into action representations, harming robustness and downstream control; this work prevents that leakage and focuses learning on action-relevant state transitions.
method: Leakage-free state prediction: train a predictor to forecast target-encoder latents while blocking information flow (stop-grad / bottleneck) so predictions must capture dynamics, not pixels.
JEPA-style latent world model: operate entirely in compact latent space (no pixel reconstruction), conditioning predictions on past observations and actions to model transitions.
Action-focused objective design: losses and architectural choices prioritize transition-consistent features and mitigate appearance/nuisance motion influence during pretraining.
impact: By shifting pretraining to leakage-resistant latent prediction, VLA-JEPA yields representations that better reflect controllable dynamics — improving robustness and transfer for downstream vision-language-action tasks and policy learning.

paper_title: VLA-JEPA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Model with Latent World Model
paper_authors: Jingwen Sun, Wenyao Zhang, Zekun Qi, Shaojie Ren, Zezhi Liu
